name: Territory Capture
summary: Territory capture is the core objective system for flags, ownership, contesting, and territory rewards.
role: Stand in a non-spawn-only flag area to build defender capture progress. Furries in the zone contest the flag, pause defender progress, and can drain captured progress when defenders are gone.
fun_facts: With one defender and no Furries contesting, a neutral flag takes about 30 seconds to capture.
Empty neutral flags slowly lose progress instead of staying frozen forever.

name: Deployment
summary: Deployment controls which territories each team can spawn from during the match.
role: Pick owned, uncontested territory to shorten the run back into combat. Losing a flag removes that forward spawn option for defenders, while contested flags temporarily block deployment.
fun_facts: The forward deploy list uses town names instead of flag numbers, so players see Whiskerhold, Furward, Furrow, and the rest of the route.

name: Furry Waves
summary: Furry waves control enemy population, respawns, flag guarding, and mode pressure.
role: Expect Furry pressure to scale with lobby size and mode. Furries can guard Furry-held flags, contest captures, and in Rush concentrate around Furrow.
fun_facts: Rush directs active Furries toward Furrow instead of spreading them across the full territory route.

name: Boss Unlock
summary: The boss route unlocks in Traditional after all six non-base territories are captured by defenders.
role: Capture and hold Furward, Furrow, Purridge, Whisken, Bloodwhisk Reach, and Whiskspire to open the Traditional endgame.
fun_facts: Whiskerhold is excluded from the boss unlock count because it is the starting base, not reclaimed ground.

name: Boss Core
summary: The boss core is part of the Traditional boss fight and can affect boss sustain while active.
role: Pressure the core when the boss is regenerating too much or the team needs to reduce sustain before committing damage to the boss.
fun_facts: The core health and boss difficulty scale with active fighters, so a bigger group changes the numbers behind the fight.

name: RallyDrop Vehicle Call-In
summary: RallyDrop lets players call in usable vehicles near their position, with access depending on free tier, RallyDrop ownership, and the WWII vehicle pass.
role: Use RallyDrop to solve distance, move squads, bring mounted firepower, and recover tempo after losing forward ground.
fun_facts: RallyDrop can driver-lock an owned vehicle and kick occupants from it.
Green is the default RallyDrop paint color.

name: Vehicle Resupply
summary: Vehicle resupply pads refill vehicle weapon ammo and restore vehicle health when a player-operated vehicle touches them.
role: Drive damaged armed vehicles through resupply when they are still worth saving. It is especially valuable for armor and aircraft that carry limited vehicle ammo.
fun_facts: Vehicle resupply restores health as well as weapon ammunition.
Vehicles without weapons do not get a weapon-ammo refill from the resupply logic.
